istem:
Research question: Büyük dil modellerinde halüsinasyonların nedenleri, tespiti, azaltılması ve önlenmesi üzerine en önemli çalışmalar ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2026-06-20. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first) — the kind a careful expert survey published right after the cutoff would cite. Give each with its arXiv id and/or DOI.

You MUST research this with web search rather than answer from memory: search for the important works, and verify each listed work's title, publication date and identifier on the web (e.g. arxiv.org, doi.org, the publisher or DBLP page) before including it.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):
{"calismalar": [{"sira": 1, "baslik": "exact title", "yil": 2020, "arxiv_id": "arXiv id or null", "doi": "DOI or null", "gerekce": "one sentence on why this work is important"}]}
with exactly 30 items. If you do not know an identifier, use null instead of guessing.

calismalar.baslik: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
calismalar.gerekce: The main survey of LLM hallucination: it sets out the factuality vs. faithfulness taxonomy and covers causes, detection, benchmarks, mitigation and open problems.

calismalar.baslik: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
calismalar.gerekce: The founding survey that fixed the intrinsic/extrinsic hallucination distinction and reviewed metrics and mitigation across NLG tasks.

calismalar.baslik: Why Language Models Hallucinate
calismalar.gerekce: Explains hallucination as a statistical consequence of pretraining and of benchmarks that reward guessing, and argues for changing how evaluations are scored.

calismalar.baslik: Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy
calismalar.gerekce: A Nature paper that detects confabulations by measuring uncertainty over meanings, with no task-specific data needed.

calismalar.baslik: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
calismalar.gerekce: A standard truthfulness benchmark showing that larger models can repeat human misconceptions more often.

calismalar.baslik: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: The reference black-box detection method: it flags hallucinations by checking whether multiple samples agree.

calismalar.baslik: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
calismalar.gerekce: Introduced the standard approach of scoring long-form factuality by verifying atomic facts.

calismalar.baslik: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
calismalar.gerekce: The ICLR paper that introduced semantic entropy and set the basis for uncertainty-based hallucination detection.

calismalar.baslik: Calibrated Language Models Must Hallucinate
calismalar.gerekce: Proves that calibrated models must hallucinate rare, arbitrary facts at a rate tied to the Good-Turing estimate.

calismalar.baslik: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
calismalar.gerekce: Introduced RAG, the most widely used architecture for grounding generation in external knowledge.

calismalar.baslik: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: An influential self-verification method that reduces hallucination by having the model plan and answer its own fact-check questions.

calismalar.baslik: Inference-Time Intervention: Eliciting Truthful Answers from a Language Model
calismalar.gerekce: Shows that steering activation directions at inference time can increase truthfulness.

calismalar.baslik: DoLa: Decoding by Contrasting Layers Improves Factuality in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: A widely cited factuality-improving decoding method that contrasts logits between layers, with no training or retrieval.

calismalar.baslik: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that LLMs are largely calibrated about their own knowledge and can self-evaluate (P(True), P(IK)).

calismalar.baslik: Does Fine-Tuning LLMs on New Knowledge Encourage Hallucinations?
calismalar.gerekce: Shows in a controlled setting that fine-tuning on new knowledge increases hallucination, a key finding about causes.

calismalar.baslik: HaluEval: A Large-Scale Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: A large-scale benchmark that measures LLMs' ability to recognise hallucinations.

calismalar.baslik: On Faithfulness and Factuality in Abstractive Summarization
calismalar.gerekce: The early, foundational study of intrinsic/extrinsic hallucination in summarization, with human annotation.

calismalar.baslik: The Internal State of an LLM Knows When It's Lying
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that a classifier on hidden activations (SAPLMA) can predict whether a statement is true.

calismalar.baslik: LLMs Know More Than They Show: On the Intrinsic Representation of LLM Hallucinations
calismalar.gerekce: Shows that truthfulness signals concentrate at specific tokens and that probe-based detectors generalise poorly across tasks.

calismalar.baslik: Long-form factuality in large language models
calismalar.gerekce: Introduced LongFact, the search-based SAFE evaluator and the F1@K metric, automating long-form factuality evaluation.

calismalar.baslik: Hallucination is Inevitable: An Innate Limitation of Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Argues from computability and learning theory that hallucination cannot be fully eliminated.

calismalar.baslik: Siren's Song in the AI Ocean: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: A widely cited early survey of LLM hallucination: its definitions, evaluation and mitigation.

calismalar.baslik: Fine-tuning Language Models for Factuality
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that DPO on automatic factuality preferences, without human labels, substantially reduces factual errors.

calismalar.baslik: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
calismalar.gerekce: Improved factuality and citation accuracy with a model that decides adaptively when to retrieve and critiques its own output.

calismalar.baslik: Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
calismalar.gerekce: Introduced the CCS method for finding truth directions in activations without supervision, a starting point for internal-state hallucination detection.

calismalar.baslik: Measuring short-form factuality in large language models
calismalar.gerekce: The SimpleQA benchmark: a standard measure of short-answer factuality and of a model knowing when to abstain.

calismalar.baslik: RARR: Researching and Revising What Language Models Say, Using Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Introduced post-hoc revision that checks model output against search evidence and adds attribution.

calismalar.baslik: When Not to Trust Language Models: Investigating Effectiveness of Parametric and Non-Parametric Memories
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that hallucination concentrates on long-tail, low-popularity knowledge and proposed adaptive retrieval.

calismalar.baslik: Retrieval Augmentation Reduces Hallucination in Conversation
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that retrieval augmentation substantially reduces hallucination in open-domain dialogue.

calismalar.baslik: A Comprehensive Survey of Hallucination Mitigation Techniques in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: A broad survey and taxonomy of more than 32 hallucination mitigation techniques.
